page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8ae.large is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor operating at 3.4 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. It includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile. The single-core CPU performance is strong, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the top 25% at 3111.99. However, multi-core and parallel processing capabilities are limited by the 2-vCPU hardware constraint, as evidenced by a weak multi-core stress-ng score of 3112.6 and a weak Geekbench multi-core score of 2448.0. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average, measuring 45.05 GB/sec for read-only and 26.33 GB/sec for write operations, while small-block cached read bandwidth is weak at 153.11 GB/sec. Complex workloads such as software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations score in the weak to poor categories, with Passmark database operations ranking in the bottom 10%.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.r8ae.large is its high memory capacity relative to its limited compute resources. While single-threaded tasks benefit from the 3.4 GHz AMD EPYC processor, multi-threaded throughput is constrained. From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a low-cost entry point into a memory-optimized hardware class, providing dedicated CPU allocation and 16.0 GB of RAM without the expense of larger multi-core instances. It is suited for workloads requiring moderate memory capacity but low parallel processing demands, such as light caching layers, single-threaded data processing, basic text processing, and low-traffic web serving.
